limitations: Finite-group result invariants do not certify all constructor/conversion protocols, inherited Basic methods or every invalid input. Comparative complexity certification remains pending.

records.invariant_argument: Every stored transversal sends its base point to its dictionary key and fixes the earlier base points. Appending generators closes each orbit by BFS while retaining valid earlier representatives. The queued rectangles cover every orbit-point/generator pair exactly once as those two lists grow. For a pair (beta,g), U_beta*g*U_(beta*g)^-1 fixes the current base point. Sifting divides out successive transversal representatives. A nonidentity residue either expands a deficient orbit or supplies a moved point extending the base. At termination every Schreier generator lies in the next stabilizer, so Schreier lemma proves each stabilizer level and the final trivial stabilizer. Orbit-stabilizer then proves that the product of basic orbit lengths is exactly the group order. Sifting to identity is consequently equivalent to group membership.
records.precision: Exact finite image arrays and unbounded Python integers; no numerical approximation or element-count cutoff.
records.complexity: For degree n and m initial generators, at most O(n^2) successful extensions occur: each adds a new point to a deficient basic orbit, or extends a base of length at most n. A level has at most m+O(n^2) generators and n orbit points. Persistent queues therefore process at most O(n^2*(m+n^2)) Schreier pairs. A pair and its sift take O(n^2) image operations. A conservative expected bound is O(m*n^4+n^6) image operations and O(m*n+n^3) stored image/index words, using amortized Python hashing. Reference incremental Schreier-Sims uses the same deficient-orbit extension criterion and restarts pair scans/rebuilds transversals after extensions. Native order/membership never enumerate all group elements. Tight comparative bounds, Python hash adversaries and integer bit costs are separate outstanding review obligations. After construction the cached exact order is returned in O(1). For one generator cycle lengths give its order by exact LCM, in O(n) image operations plus integer GCD/LCM costs. Proven named S_n/A_n orders use exact factorial arithmetic.
records.scope: All validated finite permutation generators at a common finite degree; groups built by public constructors and proven named-family factories.
records.proof_kind: human invariant argument and differential/independent closure tests; not machine-checked

records.invariant_argument: BFS starts at the supplied point, tuple or subset and repeatedly applies generators. The reached set is generator-closed. In a finite permutation group positive generator words already contain inverse actions, so this is exactly the group orbit. Unions repeat the same closure with multiple seeds.
records.precision: Exact finite image arrays and unbounded Python integers; no numerical approximation or element-count cutoff.
records.complexity: Point/union actions take O(n*m) image applications and O(n) point storage. Tuple/subset actions depend on the output orbit size and the number of supplied entries; they do not enumerate unrelated group elements. Hashing and output construction have their usual Python costs, as in the reference BFS implementation.
records.scope: Valid points, tuples or subsets with action="tuples", "sets" or "union". No certificate for arbitrary user-defined iterators.
records.proof_kind: human invariant argument and differential/independent closure tests; not machine-checked

records.invariant_argument: BFS retains the generator word reaching each first-discovered point; multiplying the parent representative by that generator sends the starting point to the new point. One representative is retained per orbit point, hence the output is exactly an orbit transversal.
records.precision: Exact finite image arrays and unbounded Python integers; no numerical approximation or element-count cutoff.
records.complexity: At most n points and n*m point actions. At most n representative products of n images, giving O(n*m+n^2) image work and O(n^2) image storage; matches the reference representative-BFS bound.
records.scope: Valid point and pairs=False/True; representative choices may differ.
records.proof_kind: human invariant argument and differential/independent closure tests; not machine-checked

records.invariant_argument: For a valid orbit transversal U, the products U_beta*g*U_(beta*g)^-1 fix the starting point. Schreier lemma states that those products generate its entire stabilizer. Identity products are omitted without changing the generated subgroup.
records.precision: Exact finite image arrays and unbounded Python integers; no numerical approximation or element-count cutoff.
records.complexity: Orbit-transversal work plus at most n*m products/inverses of n-image arrays, O(m*n^2) image work and output-dependent generator storage. Uses the same Schreier-generator construction as the reference; does not enumerate group elements.
records.scope: Valid point and validated finite generators; returned generating lists may differ while defining the same exact subgroup.
records.proof_kind: human invariant argument and differential/independent closure tests; not machine-checked
